Kurukshetra, a flat open plain of packed tan earth, late afternoon, dry wind from screen left; the Pandava line faces screen right, the Kaurava line faces screen left. The first charge of the battle, seen from Arjuna's chariot. Lens: 21 mm at f/5.6, eye height on the chariot, wide, deep focus, the nearest chariot large at frame right, the rest receding. Camera: static first frame of the shot. Atmosphere: thick dust thrown up by hooves and wheels, blown left to right by the wind, clods of earth in the air. Light: low late-afternoon sun from screen left about 15 degrees above the horizon, hard warm light around 3500 K, long shadows falling to screen right, natural falloff, bounce only from the dust. Colour: dust ochre, bronze, sun-faded white and deep shadow; moderate contrast, natural skin tones, light 35 mm film grain, slight lens breathing. Shot like a real camera on a real location: natural motion blur on fast movement; skin with pores, sweat, sun damage and fine hair; fabric with weight, folds and dirt at the hem; metal with scratches, dents and patina; ground churned with hoof marks and footprints; imperfect, asymmetric, uneven dust. 9:16 vertical frame.
